newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan cult guru evicted from own subway gas trial.
newsitem.headline: Japan cult guru evicted from own subway gas trial.

text.p: The doomsday cult guru accused of a deadly Tokyo subway gas attack was evicted from his own trial on Thursday when he turned the proceedings into a near-farce with repeated interruptions and incoherent remarks.
In a series of outbursts, Shoko Asahara described the trial as "ridiculous", said he was hallucinating, berated his own lawyers, and sarcastically asked the judge to send him to the gallows.
Judge Fumihiro Abe finally lost patience shortly after the start of the afternoon session, ordering Asahara out of the Tokyo District Court while the trial went on without him.

"This trial is absolutely ridiculous," Asahara, leader of the Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth Sect), shouted during the morning session as one of his top disciples, Kenichi Hirose, was questioned by his defence lawyers.
Asahara is on trial for the March 21, 1995, sarin nerve gas attack on Tokyo's subway system in which 12 people died and thousands were made ill.

Asahara asked the judge to stop his lawyers from questioning Hirose about the cult's alleged production of biological weapons containing the deadly bacteria which causes botulism, and plans to produce laser weapons capable of mass destruction.

When the lawyers asked about the production of Russian-style automatic rifles, Asahara erupted. "This is supposed to be the trial for the subway incident... This cross examination has nothing to with the sarin incident," he said.

The cult leader, unkempt in a loose fitting light-blue sweatsuit and with long, loose hair hanging down over his face, was forcibly shoved down into his seat by two guards after repeatedly standing up and interrupting court proceedings.
At one point he shouted: "Please stop. This is absolute nonsense."
When ordered by the judge to be quiet, Asahara retorted sarcastically: "Unless I retract my remarks, I'll be sentenced to death immediately?"
Asahara, whose real name is Chizuo Matsumoto, referred several times to what he said was his deteriorating mental state.
"How can you do this... make a blind man see hallucinations?" and "I don't know how long I can keep living in this situation," he said.
The 41-year-old leader of the sect also murmured several times: "I will be murdered."
Asahara's previous court appearance on October 18 also ended in uproar when he started shaking uncontrollably and asked Judge Abe to jump up and down in his seat.
He spent several days in a padded cell because of worries he would harm himself before doctors determined he could return to his normal cell.
